entities.summary: Fayaz Tepe, also Fayoz-Tepe, is a Buddhist archaeological site in the Central Asia region of Bactria, in the Termez oasis near the city of Termez in southern Uzbekistan. Located 15 km west of Termez off the main M39 highway. Bus number 15 runs past the turn-off to Fayaz Tepe, from where it is a 1 km walk without shade. The foundations of the site date to the 1st century CE, with a peak of activity around the 3rd and 4th centuries during the Kushan period, before experiencing a fatal decline around the 5th century CE, probably with the invasion of the Kushano-Sassanian, whose coinage can be found at the nearby site of Kara Tepe.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fayaz Tepe's significance lies in its well-preserved Buddhist ruins, which provide valuable insights into the Kushan period and the spread of Buddhism in Central Asia. The site's decline around the 5th century CE likely contributed to the region's cultural and religious shifts.
